title: The instrument
key_message: A hot source, an interferometer with a moving mirror, a laser acting as a ruler, a detector.
body: Inside the FTIR there is a source that heats a ceramic and sends out infrared light; an [[michelson-interferometer|interferometer]] splits the light into two beams and recombines it after a moving mirror; a [[reference-laser|red laser]] measures precisely where the mirror is; a detector (in our instrument a [[dlatgs|DLaTGS]], which works at room temperature) records how much light arrives.
for_chemists: Source: silicon carbide [[globar|globar]], about 1200 K. [[beamsplitter|Beamsplitter]] of KBr with a germanium coating (other materials for other ranges). The [[opd|path difference]] is twice the mirror displacement; the signal as a function of it is the [[interferogram|interferogram]]. The HeNe laser (632.8 nm) sets the sampling points: a very precise wavenumber scale ([[connes-advantage|Connes advantage]]).

[[spectral-resolution|Resolution]] Δν̃ ≈ 1/OPD_max. Compared with a dispersive instrument: [[fellgett-advantage|Fellgett]] (all frequencies together, less noise) and [[jacquinot-advantage|Jacquinot]] (no slits, more light). Detectors: pyroelectric [[dlatgs|DLaTGS]] at room temperature, linear; [[mct|MCT]] cooled with liquid nitrogen, faster and more sensitive. The ATR sample sits on the crystal, in the beam path.

figure.alt: Diagram of the optical bench: the source sends light to the beamsplitter; from there it goes to the fixed mirror and the moving mirror and returns; then it passes through the sample on the ATR crystal and reaches the detector. A separate laser measures the mirror position.
figure.caption: Simplified diagram of the interferometer: not to scale and not showing every mirror.

data_table.caption: Parts of the instrument and their job
rows: Sends infrared light of all colours.
Splits the light into two beams and recombines them.
Reflects one of the two beams always from the same distance.
Changes the distance of the second beam: creates the path difference.
Measures the mirror position and decides when to sample.
Absorbs part of the light in contact with the crystal.
